paper_title: Interactive Error Correcting Codes: New Constructions and Impossibility Bounds

statement: ▶ Theorem 1. For any ϵ > 0, there exists an iECC over the binary erasure channel resilient 6 to 11 − ϵ erasures, such that the communication complexity for inputs of size n is Oϵ (n) and the time complexity is polyϵ (n). We remark that our iECC achieves a lower erasure resilience than the quadratic sized iECC of [9], which is resilient to 35 − ϵ erasures. However, we believe that an iECC achieving both positive rate and 35 − ϵ erasure resilience can likely be constructed by combining ideas from this paper and [9]. Nevertheless, we leave open the existence of such an iECC.

For any ϵ > 0, there exists an iECC over the binary erasure channel resilient 6 to 11 − ϵ erasures, such that the communication complexity for inputs of size n is Oϵ (n) and the time complexity is polyϵ (n). We remark that our iECC achieves a lower erasure resilience than the quadratic sized iECC of [9], which is resilient to 35 − ϵ erasures. However, we believe that an iECC achieving both positive rate and 35 − ϵ erasure resilience can likely be constructed by combining ideas from this paper and [9]. Nevertheless, we leave open the existence of such an iECC. ▶ Remark 2. Since the original paper [10] was posted to arXiv, the work of [7] constructed a positive rate iECC resilient to 14 + 10−5 bit flip errors, thereby resolving whether iECC’s can achieve better error resilience in the case of bit flip errors as well! Since bit flip errors are stronger than erasures, their iECC is also a positive rate iECC resilient to > 12 erasures. Comparing this work with theirs, theirs works in the case of bit flips errors while ours does not, but our work achieves the higher erasure resilience. 1.2 Upper Bound on Maximal Error Resilience of iECC The current best known upper (impossibility) bound for the error resilience of an iECC (in the bit flip setting, rather than erasure setting) was given in [9], who showed that no iECC can be resilient to more than 27 adversarial errors. This upper bound came from the combination of two natural attacks, one of which is guaranteed to work no matter how the rounds in which Alice and Bob speak are distributed.
